questions.title: Start here - how a question is laid out

stem.text:
This question has **no parts to answer**, so it is just read.

Every question has a wording like this one (text, with maths between dollar signs, such as $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$, or an image), then **parts**: a number with its unit, a multiple-choice question, or a self-marked part. Open the next questions to try each kind.

Press the pen beside the title to edit a question, and the pen beside **Answers** to set or correct its answer key.

solution.text: Nothing to solve here. Check the **Notes** box below for a place to keep reminders, and press D to mark a question as difficult.

questions.notes: Notes you type here are saved in this browser and included in a backup.

questions.title: Kinematics - stopping distance of a car

stem.text: A car travelling at $90\ \text{km/h}$ brakes with a constant deceleration of $5\ \text{m/s}^2$ until it stops.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: How far does it travel while braking?

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: How long does the braking take?

questions.notes: Convert km/h to m/s before using any formula.

questions.title: Statics - tension in the cables holding a lamp

stem.text: A $50\ \text{kg}$ lamp hangs from two identical cables, each $30^\circ$ from the vertical, as shown. Take $g = 9.81\ \text{m/s}^2$.

parts.prompt: Find the tension in one cable.

questions.title: Fluids - flow rate through a pipe

stem.text: Water flows at a mean speed of $2\ \text{m/s}$ through a pipe of internal diameter $50\ \text{mm}$.

questions.title: Ideal gas - pressure after heating at constant volume

stem.text: A sealed rigid tank holds an ideal gas at $200\ \text{kPa}$ and $300\ \text{K}$. It is heated to $450\ \text{K}$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Which kind of process is this?

solution.text:
(a) The volume is fixed, so $P_2 = P_1 T_2 / T_1 = 200 \times 450 / 300 = 300\ \text{kPa}$.

(b) Constant volume is **isochoric**.

questions.title: Cycles - which statements about a Carnot cycle are true

stem.text: Select **all** the statements that are true.

options: Its efficiency depends only on the two reservoir temperatures.
No engine between the same two reservoirs can be more efficient.
It only works with an ideal gas.

solution.text: The efficiency $1 - T_C/T_H$ is independent of the working fluid, and it rejects heat to the cold reservoir like every heat engine.

stem.text: In your own words, explain what entropy measures and why it never decreases for an isolated system.

parts.prompt: Write your explanation, then compare it with the solution and mark yourself.

solution.text: Entropy measures how spread out (how many microscopic arrangements) a system's energy is. An isolated system moves towards the most probable arrangement, so its entropy never decreases.

questions.title: Conduction - heat loss through a wall

stem.text: A wall of area $10\ \text{m}^2$ and thickness $0.2\ \text{m}$ has thermal conductivity $k = 0.5\ \text{W/(m K)}$. The inside surface is at $20^\circ\text{C}$ and the outside at $0^\circ\text{C}$.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: What happens to the heat loss if the thickness doubles?

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Explain the answer to (c) using thermal resistance.

solution.text:
(a) $q'' = k \Delta T / L = 0.5 \times 20 / 0.2 = 50\ \text{W/m}^2$.

(b) $Q = q'' A = 500\ \text{W}$.

(c) Resistance is $L/(kA)$, so doubling $L$ halves the heat loss.

questions.notes: Parts of one question can mix numbers, choices and self-marked answers.
